audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagree with the page's own why-text: rows 0, 1 and 2 read Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir while whys[0..2] all say Maokai out-trades you, and row 4 reads Skill while whys[4] says Hemoplague plus sustain wins you the all-in.
audit.why: The packet chart is Maokai/Maokai/Maokai/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir/Vladimir, matching the prose row for row.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 flipped to Maokai and row 4 to Vladimir, as four matched full/content pairs in one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] gives his root cooldown as '~13s', and no other number appears on the page.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5 — the '~13s' figure matches no rank, and the ranked spread is what tells you the window shrinks as the lane goes on. Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1, Sapling Toss 18s, Bramble Smash 7s.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into spikes[2].text, spikes[0].text, dosFull[0].d and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three things. spikes[0] literally ships the author's confusion to the page: 'His Sapling Toss (W... his E) zones your last-hits and Twisted Advance (his W root)'. Nothing mentions that Maokai is untargetable during the Twisted Advance dash. And Sap Magic is described only as 'passive sustain'.
audit.why: The slot muddle is visible to a paying reader. The untargetability matters because it means the dash cannot be answered once started — you avoid it by spacing outside 525, not by reacting. And Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced every time he casts a spell OR is struck by an enemy spell, so poking him accelerates his own healing: that inverts the instinct to chip him down and is the strongest argument for Grievous Wounds here.
audit.corrected: Slots corrected to Sapling Toss (E) and Twisted Advance (W) throughout; untargetability and the 525 range stated in spikes[0].text, early, dosFull[0].d and the cooldown block; Sap Magic's spell-struck cooldown reduction written into spikes[0].text and wants.foe[1].
sources: enemyKit P/W/E text, ranges and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Nature's Grasp was described as 'a wave-clear/engage tool' with no mention that it creates an advancing wall which roots.
audit.why: It is a 3000-range advancing bramble wall — against a champion with no dash it functions as a retreat-cutter, which makes Flash the answer to the wall rather than to the damage.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text rewritten around the wall cutting your retreat.

audit.why: All three suspectNames hits (Sapling Toss, Twisted Advance twice) are false positives — both are Maokai's real ability names in Riot's data. The genuine defect in those same strings was the slot labelling, not the names.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1, 525 range — he is untargetable during the dash, so it cannot be interrupted. - Bramble Smash: 7s knockback. - Sapling Toss: 18s. - Nature's Grasp: 130s at rank 1.

edits.before: His lock-on root. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Maokai out-trades you early. His Sapling Toss (W... his E) zones your last-hits and Twisted Advance (his W root) locks you for a full Q-empowered trade, and his passive sustain lets him win extended pokes. Don't step up for a caster minion inside root range — farm at max range and give up the early stacks.
edits.after: Maokai out-trades you early. Sapling Toss (E) zones your last-hits from 1100 range and Twisted Advance (W) is an untargetable dash that roots on arrival, 14s at rank 1. Sap Magic heals him, and its cooldown drops every time your spell hits him — poke actually feeds it, so farm outside 525 and give up the stacks.

edits.before: Neither ult dominates the lane at 6 — his Nature's Grasp is a wave-clear/engage tool, not a duel button — but Hemoplague starts to matter. This is the pivot: once you have sustain and R, an all-in favours you if he wastes his root. Bait Twisted Advance, then commit.
edits.after: Neither ult dominates at 6 — Nature's Grasp is a 3000-range advancing wall that roots, so it cuts your retreat rather than duelling you; hold Flash for the wall, not the damage. Hemoplague matters more here: bait out Twisted Advance first, then commit.

Stay at max range, refuse to step into root range for a caster minion, and accept giving up early stacks to farm safely.

notes: The page repeatedly says Twisted Advance roots you 'into a full empowered-Q trade'. Riot's Bramble Smash text describes a knockback and slow with no empowerment mechanic, so I dropped the 'empowered-Q' framing rather than assert or deny a follow-up interaction I cannot verify from the kit. Following the mirror, I also did not claim saplings body-block Tides of Blood — Riot's text says enemy units block it, and whether a sapling counts as an enemy unit for that purpose is not resolvable here. It would be a genuinely useful line if the user can confirm it, since 'fight in saplings' is already listed as a don't.
